kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-01.prompt: What is the value of the expression $\dfrac{2007}{2+0+0+7}$?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-02.prompt: A robot starts walking on the table from square A2 in the direction of the arrow, as shown in the picture. It always goes forward. If it reaches a barrier, it always turns right. The robot will stop if it cannot go forward after turning right. On which square will it stop?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-03.prompt: Rose bushes were planted in a row, 2 m apart, on both sides of a road. How many bushes were planted along 20 m of the road?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-04.prompt: A regular die has a total of 7 points on any two of its opposite faces. In the figure, two regular dice are placed as shown. What is the sum of the points on all invisible faces of the dice?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-05.prompt: The points $A(2006, 2007)$, $B(2007, 2006)$, $C(-2006, -2007)$, $D(2006, -2007)$ and $E(2007, -2006)$ are plotted on a coordinate grid. Which of the segments is horizontal?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-06.prompt: A small square is inscribed in a big one, as shown in the figure. The lengths of two of the segments are given (3 units and 5 units). What is the area (in square units) of the small square?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-07.prompt: The figure is composed of white and black unit squares. What is the least number of white squares to paint black for the figure to obtain a line of symmetry?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-08.prompt: A number is called a “palindrome” if it reads the same backwards as forwards. For example, 13931 is a palindrome. What is the difference between the greatest 6-digit palindrome and the least 5-digit palindrome?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-09.prompt: Six identical circles are arranged as shown in the figure. The circles touch the sides of a large rectangle as well as each other. The vertices of the small rectangle coincide with the centres of four of the circles. The perimeter of the small rectangle is 60 cm. What is the perimeter of the large rectangle?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-11.prompt: If $x$ denotes any negative integer, which of the following expressions will always have the greatest value?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-12.prompt: Six points are chosen on two parallel lines $x$ and $y$ as follows: 4 points are on line $x$ and 2 points are on line $y$. How many triangles with their vertices among the given points are there?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-14.prompt: In the figure, $ABC$ and $CDE$ are congruent equilateral triangles. If the measure of angle $ACD$ is $80^\circ$, what is the measure of angle $ABD$?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-15.prompt: What percentage of all natural numbers from 1 to 10000 are perfect squares? (A perfect square is a number that can be written as the square of a natural number, for instance $100 = 10^2$.)

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-16.prompt: By drawing 9 lines (5 horizontal and 4 vertical) Peter can construct a table with 12 cells. If he had used 6 horizontal and 3 vertical lines, he would have constructed a table with only 10 cells. At most how many cells will there be in a table constructed with a total of 15 lines?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-17.prompt: A survey found that in 2006, $\frac23$ of all customers preferred product A, and $\frac13$ of all customers preferred product B. After a media campaign that promoted product B, a new survey in 2007 showed that $\frac14$ of the customers who previously preferred product A are now buying product B. Which of the following statements is definitely true?

choices.text: 5/12 of the customers buy product A, 7/12 buy product B.
1/4 of the customers buy product A, 3/4 buy product B.
7/12 of the customers buy product A, 5/12 buy product B.
1/2 of the customers buy product A, 1/2 buy product B.
1/3 of the customers buy product A, 2/3 buy product B.

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-18.prompt: The segments $OA$, $OB$, $OC$ and $OD$ are drawn from the centre $O$ of the square $KLMN$ to its sides, so that $OA \perp OB$ and $OC \perp OD$ (see the figure). The side of the square is 2. What is the total area of the shaded regions?

choices.text: depends on the choice of the points B and C

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-19.prompt: A broken calculator does not display the digit 1. For example, if we type in the number 3131, only the number 33 is displayed, with no spaces. Mike typed a 6-digit number into this calculator, but only 2007 appeared on the display. How many numbers could Mike have typed?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-20.prompt: It takes Angie 2 hours to walk a round trip on a route that contains a horizontal section and a slope section. On the way there she walks uphill on the slope section, and on the way back she walks downhill on the same section. If Angie's speed is 4 km/h on the flat section, 3 km/h climbing and 6 km/h going down, what is the total distance of the tour (round trip)?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-21.prompt: The first digit of a 4-digit number is equal to the number of zeros in this number. The second digit of the number is equal to the number of digits 1, the third digit is equal to the number of digits 2, and the fourth digit is equal to the number of digits 3 in this number. How many numbers have this property?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-22.prompt: The $3\times3$ table contains nine natural numbers (see the picture). Nick and Peter erased four numbers each so that the sum of the numbers erased by Nick was three times as great as the sum of the numbers erased by Peter. What number remained in the table?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-23.prompt: In the picture you can see a square tile, 20 cm × 20 cm. The design on the tile consists of two arcs of circles, as shown. If a table top with dimensions 80 cm × 80 cm is to be covered by these tiles so that some arcs connect in a curved line, what could be the maximum length of this line?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-24.prompt: A three-digit number has been divided by 9. The sum of the digits of the result was 9 less than the sum of the digits of the number. For how many three-digit numbers would this be true?

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-b1.prompt: (Bonus problem 1) Al and Bill together weigh less than Charlie and Dan; Charlie and Ed together weigh less than Frank and Bill. Which of the following sentences is certainly true?

choices.text: Al and Ed together weigh less than Frank and Dan.
Dan and Ed together weigh more than Charlie and Frank.
Dan and Frank together weigh more than Al and Charlie.
Al and Bill together weigh less than Charlie and Frank.
Al, Bill and Charlie together weigh as much as Dan, Ed and Frank.

kangaroo-ca-2007-g0708-b2.prompt: (Bonus problem 2) A positive integer $n$ has exactly 2 divisors, while the number $n+1$ has exactly 3 divisors. How many divisors does the number $n+2$ have?
